transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I'm Dr. [Name]. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Um… thank you, Doctor. I guess I’m here because I’ve been having a hard time getting past this feeling that I’ve… failed, really. As a father, and just as a useful person.

I know that sounds a bit dramatic, maybe, and I don’t want to overstate it, but it keeps going around in my head. I keep thinking I don’t deserve much of a future, and I couldn’t seem to shake it on my own.
How long have you been feeling this way?
I think… about a month now. It started around when my daughter left for college out of state. I’m not sure if that makes sense, but that’s when I really began feeling this way.
Have you noticed that you’ve lost interest in things you used to enjoy, like hobbies or spending time with family?

Yeah… I suppose I have, though I don’t want to make it sound like I’m doing nothing at all. It’s just… I used to really look forward to working on my model railway, and watching Cubs games with my daughter.

Now the trains are just sitting there half-built on the table, and even turning on a game feels kind of pointless. I don’t know if that’s the sort of thing you mean.
Do you find yourself feeling depressed most days, and does it often last throughout much of the day?

I… I don’t know if I’d say it’s depressed all day, every day. I mean, there are moments where I can sort of function and seem normal, I think.

But yes, most days it’s there… kind of sitting on me. It comes back a lot, and it can take up a good part of the day. I’m not sure if that answers it the right way.
Has this feeling of depression made it hard for you to carry out normal activities, like work, household chores, or socializing with others?

Yes… I mean, I can still do some things, so I don’t want to make it sound like I’ve completely fallen apart. But it’s been getting harder.

Bills are stacking up, and there are things around the house I keep meaning to finish, but I just… don’t follow through. I’ve also stopped going to book club and haven’t been riding with the people I used to see. I tell myself I’ll get back to it, but I don’t.

And… I’m a little embarrassed to say this, but I don’t think I should just brush it off anymore. I started organizing my finances in a way that felt like… like someone else might need to understand them. I don’t know if that’s the kind of thing you’re asking about.
Have you had any thoughts about not wanting to live or wished you were dead?

I… yes. I’m sorry, that’s hard to say.

It’s not like I want to upset anyone or make it sound dramatic, but I have had thoughts like… it might be easier if I just didn’t wake up. And I got scared when I realized I was going through my finances almost like I was trying to make things clear for someone else.

I don’t know if I’m saying that the right way, but… yes, I’ve had those thoughts.
Have you noticed that you're feeling more tired or that you're lacking energy, even if you haven't been doing much physically?

Yes… I think so. I mean, I haven’t been doing much that should make me tired, so it feels a little ridiculous to say, but even small things feel heavy.

Like carrying laundry upstairs, or even just sorting through the mail… it’s like I’m moving through wet cement. And it doesn’t really seem to matter how long I’ve been in bed. I still feel drained. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Have you noticed any changes in your appetite or weight recently, like not wanting to eat or losing weight without trying?

Yes… I suppose there has been some change. I hadn’t really wanted to make a big thing of it, because it sounds like I’m just not taking care of myself properly.

Most days I don’t really make a proper meal. I’ll mean to, but then I just sort of forget or put it off until late, and by then I only manage something like toast or cereal. And my belt’s been looser — I’ve had to tighten it a notch.

I’m not trying to lose weight or anything. It’s just… eating feels like one more thing I don’t quite get around to. Is that helpful to know?
Have you ever felt this way before, where you’ve had these kinds of thoughts or struggled with your mood for a long period of time?

I don’t think it’s been like this before, not really… at least not for this long.

This has been going on about a month, I’d say. It seemed to start after my daughter left for college out of state. I know that’s supposed to be a good thing, and I’m proud of her, so I feel a bit silly saying it like that… but that’s when I noticed it settling in and not really lifting. Does that make sense?
Have you ever had a period in your life before this one, lasting at least a couple of weeks, where you felt down, lost interest in things, or struggled with your mood in a similar way?

Not that I can really point to, no. I mean, I’ve had bad weeks like anyone, I suppose — stressful times, being disappointed, things like that — but I don’t remember anything lasting a couple of weeks or more in this same sort of way.

At least… not enough that I thought of it as a real problem before. Does that answer what you’re asking?

Have you ever had a time in your life before this past month when you felt down or lost interest in things for more than just a few days — maybe even weeks — in a way that felt like it was really affecting your life?

I don’t think so… I’m sorry if I’m not being clear. I’ve had low patches before, of course, but I can’t really remember a time before this where it went on for weeks and actually got in the way of my life like this.

Maybe I just didn’t think about it in those terms before, but nothing really stands out to me. Is that the sort of thing you mean?

Before this past month, have you ever had a period of time — lasting at least two weeks — where you felt down most days, lost interest in things, or experienced similar struggles with your mood that affected your daily life?

No, I don’t think so. I know I may be repeating myself, but before this past month I can’t really identify anything that lasted that long or affected my day-to-day life in this kind of way.

I’ve had normal ups and downs, but nothing I would describe as… this. Is that clear enough?
